author: @jeremyfowers

evidence.api_compatibility: resolved_ctx_size in GET /v1/models/<id>/options schema changes from type ["integer", "null"] to type "integer" (removed null). The previous null value indicated the auto-tune could not find sufficient memory — a bug that caused models to be refused. The fix makes it always return a valid integer (auto-computed size or fallback). This restores the behavior of v2026.43.3. Client code that explicitly checks for null would need updating, but this is a bug correction, not a breaking design change.
evidence.documentation: API docs updated: docs/api/openai.md (original PR) and docs/api/lemonade.md (backport) both have resolved_ctx_size description trimmed to remove the null case, matching the code change. The change is consistent across both doc files.
evidence.manual_release_testing: This is a regression fix — users on 128 GB Strix Halo who upgraded from v2026.43.3 to v2026.44.0 had models refuse to load. The fix restores the old behavior. No evidence anyone manually exercised a load with auto-tuned ctx_size on the affected hardware before merge. The change does touch the GET /v1/models/<model-id>/options endpoint (resolved_ctx_size now always returns an integer instead of null), so verifying the endpoint is worthwhile.
evidence.post_approval_commits: None. PR #3986 had one commit (8009cba) and @bitgamma's approval was submitted after that commit. PR #3994 (backport) was a single cherry-pick with no post-approval commits. CI passed on the merge commit.
evidence.review: Original PR #3986 had one substantive approval from @bitgamma (expertise: new backends, benchmarking, new models), who called it a quick patch and noted the NPU edge case as remote. @fl0rianr raised a concern about the NPU safety guard when memory is known to be zero, but the author agreed this should be a follow-up. No reviewer with iGPU/ROCm expertise (per contribute.md: @superm1 for ROCm, @kenvandine for Nvidia CUDA/ARM) reviewed. No inline review comments beyond AI-bot suggestions.
evidence.security: No security concerns. The change adds platform-specific memory total queries (/proc/meminfo on Linux, GlobalMemoryStatusEx on Windows) which read system info already available to the process. No credential handling, network calls, or permission changes.
evidence.tests: Unit test in test_gpu_memory_selection.cpp updated: the ROCm iGPU pool assertion now expects physical_total_gb == 0.0 instead of 8.0, confirming the pool no longer reports its GTT window as physical RAM. No end-to-end or integration test evidence on actual Strix Halo hardware.

maintainer_todos.text: On a 128 GB Strix Halo machine, start the server with a large model (e.g. gpt-oss-120b) using automatic context sizing and confirm the load succeeds and the model produces completions.
Call GET /v1/models/<model-id>/options with a model that has automatic context sizing (ctx_size = -1) and confirm the response field resolved_ctx_size is a non-null integer.

subject: fix(auto-tune): never refuse a load over a context estimate (#3986) (#3994)
summary: Restores model loading on shared-memory (iGPU/APU) systems by fixing the context-size auto-tune to use total physical RAM instead of RAM-in-use for the iGPU pool cap, and resolves short memory budgets to the fallback context size (4096 or 8192 for embeddings) rather than throwing; fixes gpt-oss-120b, Qwen3-Next-80B and Qwen3-Coder-Next on a 128 GB Strix Halo.
verdict_reason: The fix is sound and well-reviewed, but has no evidence of manual end-to-end testing on the affected hardware (128 GB Strix Halo with a large model) and shifts the resolved_ctx_size API value from nullable to always-integer.
